turns.answer_text:
**Reasoning**

- **Ligand:** L3 dominates the top of the table (98.7, 91.3, 83.9, 83.1, 80.2…). L6/L0 peak in the mid-80s; L2/L4/L1/L5 are clearly weaker. So L3.
- **Temperature:** every yield above ~50% is at 110 °C; no evidence of thermal degradation dominating for L3 at 110 °C (its long-residence 600 s runs still give 72–91%). Go to the max, 110.
- **Catalyst loading:** L3 at ~2.51 mol% gives 83.9 and 98.7 vs ~1.1–1.27 mol% giving 72–91 at 600 s. High Pd loading lets the reaction finish before catalyst decay matters. Push to the top of the range.
- **Residence time:** the key structure — at high loading/110 °C, 189.8 s gives 98.7 while 199.8 s gives 83.9 and 600 s (at lower loading) sags. This indicates an optimum near ~190 s: long enough for full conversion, short enough to avoid protodeboronation/Pd-black formation and side-products. Stay right at ~185–190 s rather than extending.

Final: ligand=L3, res_time=189, temperature=110, catalyst_loading=2.515
